title: Planet-Number-Element-Classification Mapping Table (Pancha Mahabootas Framework)
summary: Each planet is assigned a number (1-9) and associated with one of the five natural elements (Pancha Mahabootas: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, Space/Wood). Planets are also classified as good, wicked, or neutral. This table is the foundational reference for analysing major world events numerologically.
full_text: Each Planet has been assigned a number between 1 and 9 and each planet is also associated with one of the five natural elements — Earth, fire, water, air and space. Planets Sun, Moon, Jupiter and Mars are considered as good planets and planets Venus, Saturn, Rahu and Ketu are considered as wicked planets. Planet Mercury is considered to be neutral by some, good by some and wicked by some. Though Rahu and Ketu are not considered as planets, they have a huge role to play in our life and therefore they have been assigned a number and are associated with an element. Sun=1/Fire/good; Moon=2/Water/good; Jupiter=3/Space-Wood/good; Rahu=4/Earth/wicked; Mercury=5/Earth/good-or-neutral; Venus=6/Water/wicked; Ketu=7/Silver Metal/wicked; Saturn=8/Air-Earth/wicked; Mars=9/Fire/good.

result.note: ELEMENT SYSTEM NOTE: This table uses the Indian Pancha Mahabootas (5 elements: Earth, Fire, Water, Air, Space). This is DISTINCT from the Chinese Wu Xing (5 elements: Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal, Water) used in the Lo Shu Grid (Ch06/Ch18). Engine must not conflate these two element systems. Cross-reference: Ch18 Lo Shu groups use Wood/Earth/Fire/Water/Metal; Ch19 uses Space-Wood/Fire/Water/Air-Earth/Silver-Metal.

title: Multi-Factor Major Event Analysis Framework
summary: Analysing any major event (war, disaster, catastrophe) requires five factors: (1) the day's basic number, (2) the destiny number of the event date, (3) the year number, (4) the name number of the country/place involved, and (5) the name number of the key person/leader responsible. All five must be considered together.
full_text: The day, The destiny number (sum total of day + month + year), The Year, The country and the main person or people responsible for the events all should be considered while analysing any major event. For example, the name numbers of Adolf Hitler and Germany both should be considered while analysing world war 2, along with the day, month and the year of commencement of world war 2.

analysis_factors: Day basic number (day digit reduced to single digit)
Event destiny number (day + month + full year, fully reduced)
Year number (year digits summed and reduced)
Key person/leader name number (Chaldean, Ch08 table)
result.note: All five factors must be evaluated together. No single factor alone is sufficient for a complete event analysis. The combination of wicked/good planets across all factors reveals the numerological pattern of the event.

title: War Inference Principles — Wicked Planets, Country Groupings and Dharma War Exception
summary: Five inference principles for war analysis: (1) Wicked planets predominantly instigate wars; (2) People governed by wicked planets are mostly responsible for starting wars; (3) During wars, countries governed by good planets tend to group against those governed by wicked planets; (4) If a good-planet country appears to start a war, examine the ruling leader's number; (5) A good-planet country with a good-planet leader starting a war signals a Dharma war — destruction of evil forces.
full_text: It is mostly the wicked planets which instigate, provoke and start a war in quest for power, territory, wealth etc. It is people governed by wicked planets who are mostly responsible for starting wars. During a war, generally Countries governed by good planets group against the countries which are governed by wicked planets. If you find a country governed by good planets responsible for starting a war, then you have to see the number of the leader ruling that country. It is very rare that a country with a name number governed by good planet and ruled by a leader who is also ruled by a good planet starts a war, if it still occurs, that means, it is a war to establish Dharma, for the destruction of the evil forces.
